summary: No blocking findings discovered in the inspected workspace. The shipped round meets the iteration scope I verified: tests and static build pass, 6 compact candidates still render with correct `1탱 2딜 2힐` structure and hidden balance numbers, preference-point edits now recompute results and can change surfaced fully tied candidates, and saved-player save/load/delete flows plus docs are aligned with the current non-blocking browser-smoke policy.
strengths: `npm test` passed across all 8 test files, and `npm run build` regenerated a static `dist/` bundle with the expected entrypoint and assets.

Independent runtime checks confirmed 6 visible candidates, 113,400 total valid assignments for the sample fixture, no duplicate player assignment inside a candidate, and ordering that still respects total score difference, role-score-difference sum, tank difference, then unranked difference.

`src/lib/optimizer.js`, `src/lib/appFlow.js`, and the regression tests now show preference points influencing surfaced candidates only inside fully tied balance buckets, while preference edits trigger a full candidate/editor recompute.
Saved-player workflows are implemented and verified: v1-to-v2 migration, exact-10 load gating, individual delete, clear-all delete, Korean name-first list UI, and textarea rehydration on load.

`README.md` and `FINAL_OUTPUT.md` match the shipped workflow and accurately disclose that real Chromium-based browser smoke could not be executed in this sandbox and is non-blocking for this iteration.
verification_run: `npm run test:browser` (fails in this sandbox because no Chromium-family browser is installed; current spec marks this gap non-blocking)
`node --input-type=module` script to compare sample-fixture candidates before/after extreme preference edits and confirm surfaced candidate IDs change while balance metrics stay tied

`node --input-type=module` script using `enumerateValidAssignments(...)`, `getTopCandidates(...)`, and `compareCandidateMetrics(...)` to verify total candidate count, top-6 size, role shape, uniqueness, and ordering
`node --input-type=module` script using `buildBalanceFromClipboard(...)` and `renderResult(...)` to confirm 6 candidates render and score labels remain hidden
release_readiness: Release-ready for this iteration. Residual risk remains around unexecuted real-browser smoke because this environment has no Chromium-family browser, but that gap is explicitly documented and non-blocking under the current spec.
